title: sparse-token-trajectory-simulator-and-adaptive-slot-occupancy-reporter
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: tail-latency attribution for sequence workloads often requires understanding per-token occupancy across concurrent slots. Existing runners model aggregate token bursts but do not capture sparse token trajectories that arise from multi-turn chat mixes and mixed-length prompt priming. This PR adds a lightweight deterministic Sparse Token Trajectory Simulator (STTS) plus an Adaptive Slot Occupancy Reporter (ASOR) that produces compact per-epoch occupancy heatmaps and an occupancy->p95 cost attribution CSV for downstream analysts. Motivation: provide a reproducible micro-benchmark to validate KV-cache spill behavior, concurrency-driven kernel saturation, and the effectiveness of slot-aware packing/batching logic. Changes: 1) new simulation core (benchmark-lab/src/sim/sparse_trajectory.py) implementing deterministic pseudo-random sparse token emissions with configurable auto-correlation, priming depth, and inter-token jitter; 2) occupancy modeling module (benchmark-lab/src/reporting/slot_occupancy.py) that turns simulated timelines into epoched heatmaps and normalized occupancy histograms; 3) CLI harness (benchmark-lab/bench-tools/stts_cli.py) to run scenarios, seed profiles, and export results (CSV/JSON/FTS compressed); 4) a test corpus of representative seed profiles derived from prod-sampled session traces (benchmarks/fixtures/sparse_profiles/*.json) with associated baseline golden outputs; 5) two new CI jobs (ci/benchmark-stts.yml and ci/report-validator.yml) to run quick smoke and nightly thorough runs; 6) dashboards: example Grafana panels and JSON model for local dev (bench-dash/slot-occupancy.json). Backwards compatibility: no changes to existing runners or public APIs. This is strictly additive and guarded behind the new "stts" experiment flag in the bench-config. How to run locally: python3 -m bench-tools.stts_cli --profile=sparse_midsize --epochs=100 --out=outdir Usecases validated in this PR: - Verifies that packing logic reduces slot occupancy p95 by ~18% for the sparse_midsize profile when using slot-aware packing vs naive batching (see results below) - Demonstrates a KV-cache spill pattern that correlates with short-lived kernel saturation at 95% occupancy for long prompt priming depths - Produces compact occupancy artifacts useful for offline clustering and delta-analysis CI / testing notes: smoke job runs quick synthetic profiles (epochs=10) and compares generated CSV to golden snapshot (benchmarks/fixtures/goldens/*). Nightly job runs the full 100-epoch suite and uploads artifacts to GCS; results are parsed by the reporting validator to detect quantile regressions. Security: no sensitive data included; seed profiles are anonymized and synthetic. Checklist: - [x] Simulator core implemented and unit-tested - [x] Reporter outputs CSV/JSON/FTS and unit-tests validate schema - [x] CLI + basic documentation in bench-tools/README.md - [x] CI jobs added and flakey-tolerance configured - [x] Example Grafana panels included - [x] Linear tickets linked Related work: follows patterns from ENG-3371 (phase-aware batcher) and complements the session-trajectory compiler from pr-479913. Results summary: local validation run (sparse_midsize, epochs=100) produced occupancy p95 reduction of 18.4% when packing enabled; end-to-end latency tail reduction observed in the micro-run: p99 down 6%, p95 down 12% (see artifacts/outdir/summary.csv). Notes on determinism: simulator uses a fixed LCG seed per profile with deterministic emission rules; platform-level nondeterminism (thread scheduling) is minimized by running the simulation single-threaded by default. Next steps: add a version that can inject synthetic KV-cache misses and wire this into the kernel hint indexer for correlation testing (ENG-4620).

review_comments: Miguel Torres (reviewer): Nice work. A couple of questions: 1) can you explain why you chose the LCG instead of xorshift here? 2) please make sure the nightly job artifact retention is at least 14 days in CI.

Asha Patel (author): Response: LCG chosen for compact determinism across Py versions; added comment linking to reproducibility note and a test that exercises multiple seeds to validate distribution. Nightly retention bumped to 30d in ci/report-validator.yml.

Lena Cho (reviewer): The CSV schema looks fine; please add a short README snippet describing the column units and the expected value ranges. Also please squash small helper functions in slot_occupancy.py into a helper module to avoid duplication.
Asha Patel (author): Added bench-tools/docs/occupancy_schema.md and factored helpers into benchmark-lab/src/reporting/_helpers.py as requested.
release_notes: Add deterministic sparse token trajectory simulator and adaptive slot occupancy reporter for micro-benchmarking KV-cache and packing effects. Includes CI jobs and example dashboards. Useful for regression detection and tail latency attribution.
summary_of_results: Local 100-epoch run for sparse_midsize: slot-aware packing reduces occupancy p95 by 18.4%; end-to-end micro-run p95 latency reduced 12%, p99 reduced 6%. Artifacts stored under gs://redwood-benchmarks/stts/607721/
